summary: PRCSEQ00 is a callable Process Sequence Manager that orchestrates the running order of a batch job stream for a given process date. It is invoked with a function code and manages two indexed files: a process-sequence definition file (PRCSEQ, holding each process's id, type and dependencies) and the shared batch-control file (BCHCTL, holding per-job status). Functions: INIT builds an in-memory sequence table for the date's processes and creates 'ready' control records for each; NEXT finds the next ready process, checks its dependencies (hard vs soft, and predecessor return codes) and, if satisfied, marks it active with a start timestamp; STAT refreshes the sequence table from the control file and tallies active/error counts; TERM computes a final status (error / warning / success) and closes files. It is the batch scheduler/dependency engine of the system.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SELECT CASE function
  WHEN 'INIT': CALL 1000-INITIALIZE-SEQUENCE
  WHEN 'NEXT': CALL 2000-GET-NEXT-PROCESS
  WHEN 'STAT': CALL 3000-CHECK-STATUS
  WHEN 'TERM': CALL 4000-TERMINATE-SEQUENCE
  ELSE: SET error 'Invalid function code'; CALL 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
END SELECT
SET job RETURN-CODE = LS-RETURN-CODE; RETURN (GOBACK)

annotations.note: Called as a sub-routine (USING LS-SEQUENCE-REQUEST) — the scheduler service other jobs call.

paragraphs.name: 2000-GET-NEXT-PROCESS
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CALL 2100-FIND-NEXT-READY
CALL 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES
IF LS-RETURN-CODE = 0 THEN CALL 2300-UPDATE-PROCESS-STATUS END IF

paragraphs.name: 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET ERR-PROGRAM = 'PRCSEQ00'; SET LS-RETURN-CODE = error
CALL 'ERRPROC' PASSING ERR-MESSAGE

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.pseudocode:
OPEN PROCESS-SEQ-FILE (I-O); IF status<>'00' -> error
OPEN BATCH-CONTROL-FILE (I-O); IF status<>'00' -> error

paragraphs.name: 1200-BUILD-SEQUENCE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CLEAR WS-PROCESS-TABLE and WS-PROCESS-COUNT; SET table index = 1
SET PSR-KEY = LS-PROCESS-DATE
START PROCESS-SEQ-FILE at KEY >= PSR-KEY  (INVALID KEY -> 'No sequence found' error)
WHILE file not at end DO
  READ next record
  IF at end THEN mark status '10'
  ELSE IF PSR-TYPE = requested sequence type THEN CALL 1210-ADD-TO-SEQUENCE
END WHILE

annotations.note: START + READ NEXT = a keyed browse: position at the date, then read forward selecting matching process types.

paragraphs.name: 1210-ADD-TO-SEQUENCE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
INCREMENT WS-PROCESS-COUNT
SET table row: proc-id = PSR-PROCESS-ID, seq = count, status = READY
SET table index UP BY 1

annotations.note: Loads into a 100-row table (WS-PROC-ENTRY OCCURS 100) — more than 100 matching processes would overflow the table with no bounds check.

paragraphs.name: 1300-CREATE-CONTROL-RECORDS
paragraphs.pseudocode:
FOR each process in the table (1..WS-PROCESS-COUNT) DO
  CLEAR BATCH-CONTROL-RECORD
  SET BCT-JOB-NAME = proc id, BCT-PROCESS-DATE = date, BCT-SEQUENCE-NO = seq, BCT-STATUS = READY
  WRITE the control record  (INVALID KEY -> 'Error creating control record' error)
END FOR
paragraphs.notes: Seeds one 'ready' control record per scheduled process.

paragraphs.name: 2100-FIND-NEXT-READY
paragraphs.pseudocode:
FOR each row (1..count) DO
  IF row status = READY THEN
    SET LS-NEXT-PROCESS = row proc id
    EXIT loop
  END IF
END FOR
IF none found (index past count) THEN SET LS-NEXT-PROCESS = spaces

paragraphs.name: 2200-CHECK-DEPENDENCIES
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET PSR-PROCESS-ID = LS-NEXT-PROCESS
READ PROCESS-SEQ-FILE (INVALID KEY -> 'Process definition not found' error)
FOR each dependency (1..PSR-DEP-COUNT) DO
  CALL 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS
  IF LS-RETURN-CODE <> 0 THEN EXIT loop END IF
END FOR

paragraphs.name: 2210-CHECK-DEP-STATUS
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET BCT-JOB-NAME = dependency id; SET BCT-PROCESS-DATE = date
READ BATCH-CONTROL-FILE (INVALID KEY -> 'Dependency record not found' error)
IF dependency NOT done THEN
  IF dependency is HARD THEN SET LS-RETURN-CODE = warning END IF
ELSE
  IF dependency's return code > allowed max THEN SET LS-RETURN-CODE = error END IF
END IF
branches: IF NOT BCT-STATUS-DONE + IF hard dep -> warning
ELSE IF dep return code too high -> error

annotations.note: Core dependency rule: a not-yet-done HARD predecessor blocks (warning); a done predecessor whose return code exceeds the allowed threshold fails (error). Soft, not-done dependencies are allowed to proceed.

paragraphs.notes: The heart of the dependency engine.

paragraphs.name: 2300-UPDATE-PROCESS-STATUS
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET BCT-JOB-NAME = next process; SET BCT-PROCESS-DATE = date
READ BATCH-CONTROL-FILE (INVALID KEY -> error)
SET BCT-STATUS = active
ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIME FROM TIME STAMP; SET BCT-START-TIME = WS-CURRENT-TIME
REWRITE the control record (INVALID KEY -> error)
paragraphs.notes: Marks the chosen process active and stamps its start time.

paragraphs.name: 3100-READ-CONTROL-STATUS
paragraphs.pseudocode:
SET BCT-JOB-NAME = next process; SET BCT-PROCESS-DATE = date
READ BATCH-CONTROL-FILE (INVALID KEY -> 'Process record not found' error)

paragraphs.name: 3200-UPDATE-SEQUENCE-TABLE
paragraphs.pseudocode:
FOR each row (1..count) DO
  IF row proc-id = BCT-JOB-NAME THEN
    SET row status = BCT-STATUS; SET row rc = BCT-RETURN-CODE
    EXIT loop
  END IF
END FOR
paragraphs.notes: Syncs the in-memory table with the persisted control record.

paragraphs.name: 3300-CHECK-COMPLETION
paragraphs.pseudocode:
RESET WS-ACTIVE-COUNT = 0, WS-ERROR-COUNT = 0
FOR each row (1..count) DO
  IF row status = ACTIVE THEN INCREMENT WS-ACTIVE-COUNT END IF
  IF row status = ERROR  THEN INCREMENT WS-ERROR-COUNT  END IF
END FOR

paragraphs.name: 4100-CHECK-FINAL-STATUS
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CALL 3300-CHECK-COMPLETION
IF WS-ERROR-COUNT > 0 THEN SET LS-RETURN-CODE = error
ELSE IF WS-ACTIVE-COUNT > 0 THEN SET LS-RETURN-CODE = warning
ELSE SET LS-RETURN-CODE = success
END IF
branches: ELSE IF any still active -> warning
paragraphs.notes: Overall run verdict for the sequence.

paragraphs.name: 4200-CLOSE-FILES
paragraphs.pseudocode:
CLOSE PROCESS-SEQ-FILE and BATCH-CONTROL-FILE
IF either close status <> '00' THEN SET error 'Error closing files'; CALL 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE END IF
